messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: shinyRGL issue
parts:
Hi,

1) I have an app that uses shinyRGL running on shiny server pro. It was working fine yesterday. Today it gives the error: rgl.open failed. The only thing that changed, is that I installed ggvis on the server installation of R. The shinyRGL app runs fine when I run it local in a Chrome browser (also with the new ggvis installed on the local computer).

2) When I run the shinyRGL app in rstudio using runApp(launch.browser = rstudio::viewer), I get the error "your browser does not support webgl". 

#1 is much more critical than #2. I haven't been able to find much relavent to either issue on google. I did try adding options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) to server.R as recommended by the shinyRGL help page, but this did not fix the problem.


Jonathan

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: shinyRGL issue
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

Regarding #2, it seems that the viewer we use unfortunately doesn't support WebGL. Perhaps a later version will, but for now you'll just need to open the app in a "real" browser like Chrome or Firefox.

About #1, I'm not sure what the issue would be, but I doubt that the mere presence of ggvis would upset shinyRGL. I suspect that some package got updated as a side-effect and perhaps there's something incompatible in one of the updated packages. Can you post the version of the loaded packages (sessionInfo()) in your app when it's not working?

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: Re: shinyRGL issue
parts:
I got it working. It seems like it might be related to options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) mentioned under "running headless" in the shinyRGL doc. http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shinyRGL/README.html. 

The strange thing is that we had the option line in server.R before library(shinyRGL), and it was working fine yesterday. It seems like after I installed ggvis, it stopped working. I added the following lines in ui.R, restarted the server, and updated some toolboxes, and it started working. Unfortunately, I'm not sure which thing I did fixed the problem. 

options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE)

library(shinyRGL)

library(rgl)

I wonder if there's some kind of cross talk between apps. I thought I read somewhere that Shiny Server is efficient in recycling R processes . For example, if one app somehow happened to load RGL without this option set (for example, does loading ggvis in turns loads RGL, but doesn’t have the option set?). Then when the ECG app starts there’s already an R process running that already loaded the RGL library without the option set.

Is there some way I can force R to reload shinyRGL and RGL with the option set?

Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: shinyRGL issue
parts:
Glad to hear you got it working. I don't have any intuition about which of those might have fixed the issue.

Shiny Server will not recycle R processes for different applications -- each application gets its own isolated process. Now R will certainly make changes (I'm thinking of installing packages) that can effect other R processes. But in general you should be safe in terms of setting options or loading packages.

I'll chew on this a little more and let you know if I think of anything.

Jeff
